**Pipeline controller notification**
This repo is configured to use the [pipeline controller](https://docs.ci.openshift.org/how-tos/creating-a-pipeline/). Second-stage tests will be triggered either automatically or after lgtm label is added, depending on the repository configuration. The pipeline controller will automatically detect which contexts are required and will utilize `/test` Prow commands to trigger the second stage.

For optional jobs, comment `/test ?` to see a list of all defined jobs. To trigger manually all jobs from second stage use `/pipeline required` command.

<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/9042):

>## Summary
>
>- **Trimmed push hooks**: replaced full `make verify` + `make test` with `make verify-quick` (generate + git-clean) and `make test-changed` (tests only changed Go packages vs upstream/main). Push hooks now run in ~3-8 minutes instead of 15+.
>- **Python tooling portability**: consolidated three separate pip install recipes into a single virtualenv at `hack/tools/bin/python-venv/` using `uv` when available with `pip` fallback. Fixes macOS portability issues with bare-metal Python assumptions.
>- **Fixed trailing whitespace diff cycle**: `docs-aggregate` now strips trailing whitespace from generated `aggregated-docs.md`, preventing a perpetual diff between the docs-aggregator output and the pre-commit trailing-whitespace hook.
>- **Updated docs**: rewrote `precommit-hook-help.md` to document what runs on commit vs push, and explain that full verification runs in GHA.
>
>## Motivation
>
>Push hooks were timing out in Claude Code (10-minute bash limit), exhausting CPU/RAM on developer machines, and had Python portability issues on macOS. Full verification (staticcheck, vet, fmt, full test suite) already runs in GHA via `verify-reusable.yaml` and `test-reusable.yaml`, so push hooks only need to be a smoke check for the most common CI failures.
>
>## Test plan
>
>- [x] Fresh Python venv creation with `uv` (tested `make verify-codespell`, `make run-gitlint`)
>- [x] `make verify-quick` catches stale generated files
>- [x] `make verify-quick` passes on clean state
>- [x] `make test-changed` skips when no Go files changed
>- [x] `make test-changed` runs tests for changed packages
>- [x] Commit hooks pass on all commits
>- [x] Portable sed produces no backup files on macOS
>- [x] `default_stages: [pre-commit]` only affects hooks without explicit `stages` (all commit hooks already have `stages: [pre-commit]`)
>
>/cc @openshift/hypershift-approvers
>
>🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Pre-commit hook timing (local, Apple M3 Max)

**Commit stage** (runs on staged files only):

| Hook | Time |
|---|---|
| Check merge conflict strings | <1s |
| Check yaml syntax | <1s |
| Trailing whitespace trim | <1s |
| Codespell | ~5s |
| CPO containerfiles sync | <1s |
| Sort API imports | ~2s |
| Sort imports | ~3s |
| Gitlint | ~2s |

**Push stage** (new in this PR):

| Hook | Time |
|---|---|
| `make verify-quick` (generate + update + verify-git-clean) | ~55s |
| `make test-changed` (unit tests for changed packages only) | 0.3s (no changes) to ~30s (typical) |

Previously push hooks ran full `make verify` (~10+ min) and `make test` (~15+ min). The new push hooks complete in under 2 minutes for a typical change.
